transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been getting kind of stuck on how my face looks. Mostly around my jaw—like it’s sagging or uneven on one side. It got worse after seeing myself in some family photos. My wife says she barely notices, and clients don’t seem to either, but… I keep seeing it.
Is this concern about your face affecting your daily activities or interactions with others?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I still do my job and everything. But I’ve been taking longer to leave for client meetings, checking myself more than I should. Sometimes during appointments I’m not really as focused.

And I’ve skipped a few art openings lately… just didn’t want to be seen, or end up in photos.
Do you find yourself thinking about your face's appearance for more than an hour a day?

Yeah… probably. I don’t really time it, but I keep coming back to that sagging, uneven look around my jaw and one side of my face. Since those family photos, it’s been hard to let it go, even though my wife says she barely sees anything.
Would you say that thinking about your face's appearance is causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah… it does bother me. Maybe “a lot” sounds strong, but I keep getting stuck on it—the sagging, uneven look around my jaw, one side of my face. Ever since those family photos, it’s just… hard not to see it, even when my wife says it’s barely noticeable.
Is your concern mainly about how your face looks to others, or is it more about how you feel about your face itself?

Mostly how it looks to other people, I think. Like… when I saw those family photos, I got stuck on how uneven my jaw and one side of my face looked. My wife says she barely notices it, and clients don’t seem to either, but I still worry that they do.
Is there something specific you think would fix the way your face looks to you?

I don’t know if there’s one specific thing. I guess… if that sagging, uneven part around my jaw and one side of my face didn’t show so much, especially in photos, I’d probably feel better. But I’m not really sure what would fix it.
Do you think other people actually notice the unevenness in your face, or is it more that you're worried they might?

I guess it’s more that I’m worried they might. My wife says she barely sees anything, and clients haven’t really said anything… but I still get stuck on that sagging, uneven look around my jaw, especially since seeing those photos.
Have you been avoiding social interactions or events because of your concerns about your face?

A little, yeah. I mean, I still go to work and meet clients, but I’ve been dragging my feet more getting out the door. And sometimes during appointments I’m… not fully there.

Socially, I’ve skipped a few art openings. I just didn’t want to be seen, or end up in photos.
Is your concern about your face's appearance focused on this one issue with your jaw and the unevenness, or do you also worry about other parts of your face?

Mostly that one thing… the jaw, and how one side of my face looks kind of saggy or uneven. That’s what I keep coming back to, especially after seeing those family photos. I don’t think it’s really other features, not in the same way.
Has your concern about your face's appearance affected your relationships with family or friends?

A bit, I guess. I haven’t really stopped seeing family or friends completely, but I’ve skipped a few art openings and things like that because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. And even with work, I still go, but I’m slower getting myself out the door and not always fully present.
Have you noticed any significant problems at work or in other areas of your life because of your concerns about your face?

Nothing major, I don’t think. I’m still getting my work done.

But… yeah, it’s slowed me down some. Getting out the door for client meetings takes longer, and a few times during appointments I’ve felt kind of distracted. Outside of work, I’ve skipped some art openings because I didn’t want to be seen or photographed.
Do you think your view of your face's appearance is realistic?

I’m not sure. Part of me thinks it must be realistic because I can see it, especially in those family photos… the sagging or unevenness around my jaw. But my wife says it’s barely noticeable, and clients don’t seem to react, so… I guess I don’t really know.
Is your concern about your face's appearance still focused on the jaw and unevenness issue you mentioned earlier?

Yeah… mostly that. I keep getting stuck on the sagging, uneven look around my jaw, like one side of my face is off. It got worse after seeing myself in those family photos, even though my wife and clients say they barely notice anything.
Has your concern about your face's appearance caused you to avoid any important life events or opportunities?

I wouldn’t say big opportunities, exactly. I mean, I’m still working and showing up.

But… yeah, I’ve avoided a few things, like art openings, because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in photos. And with client meetings, I’ve been slower getting myself out the door, and sometimes I’m not as present once I’m there.
Do you think that others would notice this unevenness in your face if they looked closely?

Yeah… I think if they looked closely, they might. That’s what I get stuck on — the uneven, sagging look around my jaw, one side seeming off. My wife says people barely notice, and clients don’t seem to, but I still feel like it’s there.
Have you felt like your concerns about your face are holding you back from doing things you want or need to do?

A little, yeah. I still do what I need to for work, but it slows me down getting to client meetings sometimes, and I’m not always fully there once I’m in them.

And I’ve skipped a few art openings… mostly because I didn’t want to be seen or end up in pictures.
Do you ever find it difficult to stop thinking about the appearance of your face, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

Yeah… it is hard to drop it sometimes.

I’ll be trying to focus on work or something normal, and my mind goes back to that sagging, uneven look around my jaw, like one side of my face is off. It got worse after I saw myself in those family photos. My wife says it’s barely noticeable, and clients don’t say anything, but… I still keep thinking about it.
Do you spend more than 3 hours a day thinking about your face's appearance?

I don’t know if it’s more than three hours exactly… I haven’t really timed it.

But I do keep getting stuck on it — the sagging, uneven look around my jaw, like one side is off. Especially since seeing those family photos. Even if my wife or clients don’t seem to notice, it’s still in my head a lot.
Has your concern about your face's appearance caused significant problems in your ability to work or maintain relationships?

Some, yeah. I mean, I’m still working and handling things, but it’s made me slower getting out to client meetings, and sometimes I’m not really as present once I’m there.

With relationships… not in a big dramatic way. I’ve skipped a few art openings, though, because I didn’t want people looking at me or taking pictures.
